articles.title_orig: Nvidia Opens Investigation Into Jensen Huang’s Relationship With Chinese Spy
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Opens Investigation Into Jensen Huang’s Relationship With Chinese Spy
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia announced Sunday it is launching an independent investigation into its chief executive and founder, Jensen Huang, over concerns he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
The statement, published on the company’s website, comes after US officials have expressed concern over Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. (The two are not related).
Separately, Huang admitted having an extramarital affair in a note to staff, though he did not name the woman.
The Financial Times previously reported that US officials believed the two were in a romantic relationship. Several outlets have reported that American officials suspect Alice Huang has fed intelligence to China and helped smuggle advanced artificial intelligence chips to the country. Nvidia is the world’s leading chipmaker amid the AI boom and has a market capitalization of about $4.5 trillion.
CNN has asked the State Department for comment.
The company previously said in a statement that Jensen Huang’s meetings were “not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were “debunked last year.”
Nvidia said a committee of independent directors and outside counsel will oversee its investigation.
“The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. But, the board “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.”
“Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” a spokesperson for Nvidia told CNN.
Jensen Huang, 63, said that he was “unfaithful” and hurt his wife and children in the note to Nvidia staff.
“I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it,” Jensen Huang said, adding that he supports Nvidia’s investigation. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security.”
This is a developing story and will be updated.
CNN’s Logan Schiciano contributed to this story

articles.title_orig: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
articles.title_zh: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang "is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA," the company said.
Tech giant NVIDIA has announced an investigation of its CEO amid allegations that he was the subject of a intelligence-gathering effort by the Chinese.
"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company said in a statement Sunday, adding that a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
Jensen "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the NVIDIA statement further said.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," according to the statement.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement further said.
"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," according to the statement.
The New York Times reported late last month that Huang, who runs the world's largest computer chip manufacturer, was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot centered around a woman they identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials determined was funneling information to Beijing and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang.
The Chinese government has denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment after the New York Times story broke.
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected" and are part of Jensen Huang's job, an NVIDIA spokesperson told ABC News at the time.
However, NVIDIA on Sunday shared with ABC News an internal message Jensen Huang sent to employees, in which he said he was "unfaithful" to his wife.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the message said, in part. It did not name Alice Huang nor any other person.
Addressing NVIDIA staff, partners and shareholders, Huang went on to say "my responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," Huang's message said.
Following the New York Times report, congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China sent a letter to Jensen Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the letter said, in part. It is not known if Huang will appear before the committee.
“Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," and NVIDIA spokesperson told ABC News Sunday.

articles.title_orig: Newport Beach fishermen find Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water 20 miles off coast
articles.title_zh: Newport Beach fishermen find Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water 20 miles off coast
articles.content_orig:
Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident
A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.
The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.
Authorities believe the man may have been in the ocean for approximately nine hours before he was spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who were returning from a fishing trip near Catalina Island.
The two fishermen had spent the morning fishing for marlin when their trip took an unexpected turn. By noon, they had pulled the stranded man from the water.
“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” Garrett told CBS News , recalling the moment the boat’s captain first saw the man in the water.
The fishermen quickly worked together to bring the man onboard. Once the man regained his composure, Garrett said he identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the Ovation of the Seas.
According to Norton, the rescued crew member had few words to describe what he had just experienced. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said.
After the rescue, the fishing crew issued an emergency maritime call, prompting Newport Beach lifeguards to respond and provide assistance. Battalion chief Adam Yacenda said the man was found approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, according to CBS, or “pretty much in the middle of the ocean”.
Despite the extended time spent in the water, Norton believes unusually warm ocean temperatures may have played a significant role in the man’s survival.
“You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees,” Norton said. “A different year, no way he makes it.”
The circumstances surrounding the crew member’s fall from the cruise ship remain under investigation by the Coast Guard. Royal Caribbean Group acknowledged the incident and said it is assisting the employee following the ordeal.
In a statement to CBS, a company spokesperson said: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

articles.title_orig: Rubio oversaw classified memo alleging Nvidia CEO’s ties to suspected Chinese intelligence operative: Report
articles.title_zh: Rubio oversaw classified memo alleging Nvidia CEO’s ties to suspected Chinese intelligence operative: Report
articles.content_orig:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified intelligence memo warning senior Trump administration officials that Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang had developed a close relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative, the New York Times reported Sunday.
The warning, drafted under Rubio's supervision in the spring of this year, circulated among national security officials holding high-level clearances ahead of a bilateral state visit to China in May by US President Donald Trump.
The document stemmed from electronic surveillance targeting Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who is unrelated to the Nvidia chief. She worked as a senior executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company that purchased advanced artificial intelligence processors while under federal investigation for illicitly smuggling semiconductors into mainland China.
When intelligence officials requested the unmasking of an American citizen seen in intercepted communications showing an intimate relationship with her, the review identified the executive as Jensen Huang. Counterintelligence agencies concluded that China's Ministry of State Security had recruited Alice Huang as an operative.
Jensen Huang was initially excluded from the official business delegation traveling with Trump to China. However, after noticing media reports highlighting the absence, Trump intervened directly, arranging for Huang to rendezvous with Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska and praising him as "the Great Jensen Huang."
Trump declined to impose restrictions on Huang or the chipmaker, viewing Nvidia's market dominance as vital to US economic competition and financial markets.
Nvidia’s board of directors announced an independent investigation following the reports.
Nvidia earlier said that Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were "not unusual or unexpected," characterizing them as standard commercial engagements and noting that Megaspeed never received classified corporate data or trade secrets.
China in October rejected a related report by the New York Times, dismissing the allegations as "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but a smear against China."
The White House, the State Department and the Central Intelligence Agency declined to comment, the New York Times said, while Alice Huang did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: A Missionary Pope Faces a Chain Saw-Wielding Populist in Argentina
articles.title_zh: A Missionary Pope Faces a Chain Saw-Wielding Populist in Argentina
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV has called on Argentine President Javier Milei and the country’s political leaders to “safeguard democracy” and demonstrate a “careful use of words” during his first speech in Buenos Aires.
The American pope arrived in Argentina on Sunday, embarking on a trip that his predecessor, the first Argentine pope, was never able to make.
Leo’s highly anticipated papal visit to Argentina began with a private meeting with President Milei shortly after the pope landed. Milei has received strong backing from US President Donald Trump, with whom Leo, first American pontiff, has publicly disagreed, particularly on the treatment of migrants and the war in Iran.
The pope’s visit comes at a time when Milei’s “chainsaw” austerity measures have led to welfare spending cuts. Milei has also equated state-led social justice programs with communism and has also been accused of undermining democracy through attacks on the press and divisive rhetoric. He has also struggled to secure bipartisan agreements.
“Democracy, then, is also a part of Argentina’s heritage that needs to be safeguarded,” the pope said at a meeting with politicians, members of civic society and the diplomatic corps at the Palacio Libertad. “Democracy is also strengthened by the daily conduct of public life: through willingness to listen, through careful use of words, through the patient search for agreement, and through the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future.”
The Chicago-born pontiff, who recently cast a mail-in ballot during the US mid-term elections, talked about the importance of the “freedom to elect one’s own leaders through the ballot box.” He urged leaders to recognize the limits of their power, and said that democracy is protected by “confidence in the law”, the ability to freely express convictions and for institutions to serve all parties.
“Authority is most authentic when it is exercised as service, when it looks beyond the immediate, and when it uses its power to promote the welfare of all,” the pope said. An eruption of applause from the audience forced him to repeat his next line: “Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them.”
Leo’s November 8-11 trip is the first papal visit to Argentina in almost four decades and it comes with the added dimension that Pope Francis did not make a return trip home during his 12-year-papacy. Millions are expected to attend the various services and events while the pope is in the country.
Francis’ decision not to visit Argentina was something even his closest friends were unable to explain. Some have suggested the late pope’s reluctance to visit was linked to Argentina’s polarized political culture, with Francis wary that his presence in the country could be weaponized.
The Argentine pope had a strong emphasis on the church helping the most marginalized in society. Francis lamented Argentina’s economic decline which he blamed on decades of bad governance. He contrasted the roughly 5% inflation rate he recalled from his youth with the soaring inflation and high poverty rates of recent years.
In his speech, Leo cited Argentina’s “abundance of human resources” but called for its “wealth bear fruit for the benefit of all and warned that corruption undermines trust in institutions.
Before his election as pope in 2013, Francis served as archbishop of Buenos Aires, where he spoke out on social justice and was unafraid to criticize political leaders.
Leo’s visit, the second leg of his 12-day tour of South America, will underline the ways he continues the reforms of his predecessor, but with his own distinctive style.
Pope Leo, in contrast, has made the church’s social teaching and concern for the marginalized a central concern of his papacy. His itinerary in Argentina includes a visit to a federal prison in Buenos Aires and a stop at a care center for people with intellectual and physical disabilities in Claypole which has been affected by the Milei cuts.
During his presidential campaign and in the years leading up to it, Milei repeatedly insulted Francis, calling him an “imbecile” for defending social justice, “the representative of the evil one on earth” and a “sh*t of a pope.” Milei later apologized for these remarks and called Francis “the most important Argentine in history” following the pontiff’s death in April 2025, repeating the compliment in his remarks on Sunday.
Milei and Francis met in the Vatican in February 2024, with the pope joking with the president: “you cut your hair!” — a reference to the unruly hairstyle which earned Milei the nickname “The Wig.” Milei replied that he had “tidied it up.”
Leo and Milei previously met at the Vatican in June 2025. After meeting Milei in the Casa Rosada on his arrival in Buenos Aires, the pope was presented with the keys to the city of the Argentine capital by the mayor, Jorge Macri.
CNN’s Claudia Rebaza contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Production suspended at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field after drone attack, sources say
articles.title_zh: Production suspended at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field after drone attack, sources say
articles.content_orig:
The Khor Mor gas field, an important energy facility, was attacked Saturday. The attack came less than 24 hours after a report that the Iranian-backed group Kataib Hezbollah had made comments about the gas facility.
In the past, Iranian-backed groups have targeted the facility. The Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq and its Kurdistan Regional Government have long asked Baghdad for drone defenses to defend the gas field and other sites. Iran has carried out more than 1,000 drone and missile attacks on the Kurdistan Region since February.
Rudaw media in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region , reported that “gas production at the Khor Mor field west of Sulaimani came to a halt late Sunday after an unknown projectile struck the facility’s gas storage unit, causing significant damage, according to a Rudaw reporter on the ground.” Reports and videos online show smoke and fire billowing from the facility and the sky lit up in orange from the flames. Some reports say the facility was struck by a drone.
Rudaw added that “a source from the field confirmed the attack to Rudaw’s Peshawa Bakhtyar but couldn’t determine whether the attack came from an attack drone or a rocket, adding that the strike has caused a ‘massive fire’ in the field.”
Bakhtyar also said that the strike “hit Khor Mor’s warehouse unit, which stores nearly 1.5 thousand tons of cooking gas through 170 oil tankers. The source said the fire was close to being brought under control.” A Telegram channel linked to pro-Iran terrorist groups has said a drone was involved in the attack.
Meanwhile, on Sunday, reports noted that Abu Mujahid al-Assaf of Kataib Hezbollah had slammed Iraq’s prime minister Ali al-Zaidi and said, "we do not want to air dirty laundry in public, nor open the files of (Khor Mor) and the incitement to target it for the purpose of extorting the UAE; for whoever's house is made of glass should not throw stones at people."
The reference to Khor Mor may have been a threat. Zaidi has vowed to rein in armed groups and confiscate their weapons. Kataib Hezbollah has been in the spotlight amid this attempt to disarm various groups, including the Iranian-backed groups. Zaidi also canceled contracts at Mosul airport because the contracts were linked to “armed groups,” which is usually a euphemism for Iranian-backed terrorist groups in Iraq.
Kataib Hezbollah has targeted facilities in Iraq in the past and also targeted Saudi Arabia and killed three Americans in Jordan in January 2024. Khor Mor gas field was attacked in December 2025, February 2025 and August 2023.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus .
Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) is tightening how it tracks artificial-intelligence chips sold across Southeast Asia as pressure grows on the company to prevent restricted hardware from reaching China through intermediaries.
The chipmaker now requires buyers in the region to join its fleet intelligence tracking system if they want to become official Nvidia Cloud Partners, according to TipRanks, citing Bloomberg. The program records the physical location of AI chips inside data centers.

The incentive is meaningful.
Nvidia Cloud Partner status gives cloud companies priority access to some of Nvidia's most in-demand chips and provides a public seal of approval. Nvidia is effectively using that privilege to push more regional customers into a tracking system that had previously been voluntary.
The change comes amid mounting scrutiny from U.S. officials.
American authorities believe billions of dollars worth of restricted Nvidia chips have reached China through smuggling networks operating across Southeast Asia. In March, authorities arrested Super Micro Computer co-founder Wally Liaw on charges tied to an alleged $2.5 billion scheme to route Nvidia GPU servers into China.
Malaysia has also become a focal point. Customs authorities recently seized about $12.1 million of advanced AI chips at the country's main airport while investigating a suspected smuggling network.
Nvidia has already taken additional steps.
The company reportedly cut half of the Asian firms on its pre-approved buyer list and told cloud customers that no more than half of their Nvidia computing capacity should be rented to Chinese clients.
I think this is fundamentally a compliance-risk story rather than a demand story .
Nvidia still faces enormous demand for its chips, but the company increasingly has to prove that it knows where those chips end up.
That matters because repeated smuggling cases could give Washington justification for much tougher export restrictions, which would be far more damaging than the cost of tighter customer screening today.
The trade-off is that stricter monitoring could make Nvidia less attractive to some Southeast Asian cloud providers and complicate sales in one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure regions.
For investors, the key things to watch are whether Washington accepts Nvidia's new controls, whether more Asian customers lose approved status, how much China-related cloud demand disappears, and whether export rules tighten further .
Nvidia is trying to solve the problem before regulators solve it for them.

articles.title_orig: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.title_zh: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.content_orig:
The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.
Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike.
Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike.
The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles.
The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months.
It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people , including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen.
Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group.
Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war.
An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there.
Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

“My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Nvidia announced in a press release Sunday that its board was opening an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

CEO Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate with it, the board said.
There was no word of Huang’s position being in jeopardy, with the board saying it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”
Nvidia is one of the hottest companies in the stock market right now, given the popularity of its chips. It has a market capitalization of roughly 4.5 trillion and was trading at nearly $240 per share early last month.
Huang, like other tech leaders, has flocked to Trump as the president embraces AI. The Nvidia leader and his wife, Lori Huang, attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House in September. articles.title_orig: Iran gives US two-day diplomacy ultimatum
articles.title_zh: Iran gives US two-day diplomacy ultimatum
articles.content_orig:
Coverage for this event has ended.
President Donald Trump declined Friday to say whether the U.S. was responsible for reported missile strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, while acknowledging that American forces have conducted limited strikes against Iranian air defenses.
Asked by a reporter whether the U.S. carried out the reported strikes, Trump responded, "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes, but they knock out. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five."
Iranian state media reported that two projectiles struck the Suza area of Qeshm Island, according to Reuters.
Trump did not specify where the U.S. operation he described took place or whether it was connected to the reported strikes on Qeshm Island.
Click here to follow the latest updates in the conflict with Iran.
President Donald Trump's top advisers are divided over whether to resume military strikes against Iran or continue negotiations, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff favor diplomacy, while Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper support renewed military operations, the newspaper reported, citing U.S. officials.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly favor maintaining economic pressure through sanctions and the blockade.
The disagreements come as Trump weighs further strikes following Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The president said Friday that Iran wants to reach an agreement with Washington.
The State Department warned Americans in the Middle East on Friday to remain vigilant amid increased threats of armed attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi militants and potential targeting of U.S. government officials.
In a security alert posted on X, the department's Bureau of Consular Affairs urged Americans in the region to exercise heightened caution and prepare for possible travel disruptions.
The department warned that Iranian-backed Houthis pose an increased threat of armed attacks and that Iran is attempting to target American government officials in the region.
U.S. citizens were also advised to monitor country-specific security alerts and remain aware of potential flight cancellations and airspace closures.
The warning comes as tensions remain high across the Middle East, with President Donald Trump weighing renewed military strikes against Iran while Washington and Tehran continue diplomatic negotiations.
President Donald Trump said Friday that Iran is eager to reach an agreement with the United States, citing economic troubles and damage to Tehran's military capabilities as Washington considers its next steps in the conflict.
During a gaggle with reporters, Trump was asked who persuaded him to pursue negotiations after launching military strikes against Iran.
"Nobody," Trump responded, defending the strikes and arguing that Iran would have posed a greater threat to Israel and other countries in the region if it had obtained nuclear weapons.
"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," Trump said.
The president also pointed to Iran's economic difficulties, asserting that inflation had reached 300% and that its navy had been destroyed.
Iran is demanding concrete action from Washington before advancing nuclear negotiations, with a senior official saying Friday that Tehran will no longer rely on written U.S. commitments.
Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, accused Washington of repeatedly violating its commitments over the past 18 months, according to state-run IRNA, as reported by Iran International.
“Iran needs to see the US’s practical actions, and [then] the groundwork for opening a new chapter would be prepared,” Bagheri said.
The remarks come as Washington reviews a nuclear proposal submitted by Tehran through Qatari intermediaries, while President Donald Trump considers renewed military strikes against Iran.
The U.S. is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation assistance for information about Iran's nuclear program, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced Friday.
In a post on X, CENTCOM highlighted the State Department's Rewards for Justice program, which is seeking information about Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment and personnel involved in the program.
The reward also covers information about the movement of nuclear-related materials, equipment or personnel, including individuals in the scientific community.
The announcement comes as President Donald Trump considers renewed military strikes against Iran while Washington and Tehran continue negotiations over the country's nuclear program.
Trump reiterated Friday that Iran would never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon, pointing to previous U.S. military operations targeting Tehran's nuclear facilities.
President Donald Trump reiterated Friday that Iran would never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon, pointing to previous U.S. military strikes against Tehran's nuclear facilities.
Speaking at the UP Summit at Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, Trump credited American B-2 bombers with preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons.
"And you know what? If they did have it, if we didn't go in with those beautiful B-2 bombers a little more than a year ago, if I allowed them to have it today, there would be no Israel. It would have been wiped off the face of the earth, and there would be no Middle East," Trump said.
"We will never let that happen. Iran will never, ever have a nuclear weapon. You can rest assured," the president added.
Trump's remarks come as his administration considers renewed military operations against Iran while continuing diplomatic negotiations with Tehran over its nuclear program.
Qatar pushed back Friday against reports suggesting negotiations between the United States and Iran had collapsed, insisting that both countries are continuing efforts to reach an agreement.
In a statement, Qatar's International Media Office rejected online reports alleging that Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani had said Washington and Tehran failed to reach a deal.
The office accused unnamed parties of misrepresenting the prime minister's comments and spreading misinformation to undermine diplomatic efforts.
"His Excellency’s remarks have been deliberately distorted by those who benefit from continued war and instability in our region," the statement read. "Many of these claims are being spread by fake accounts trying to undermine diplomatic efforts and push for further escalation. This is deeply irresponsible. His Excellency stated today that both sides are continuing to work towards a deal."
Qatar said its mediators remain in close contact with both countries as negotiations continue.
Three incoming Jewish members of Congress are calling for the release of Arab journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, who was detained in Israel after interviewing a fugitive former lawmaker.
Brad Lander, Steve Weiner and Daniel Biss sent a letter to Israeli Ambassador to the U.S. Yechiel Leiter expressing concern about Abu Shehadeh's detention, according to The Times of Israel.
The journalist was arrested Tuesday after interviewing former Israeli lawmaker Azmi Bishara, who fled Israel in 2007 amid suspicions that he aided Hezbollah during the previous year's war in Lebanon.
The lawmakers said Israeli authorities detained Abu Shehadeh on suspicion of contact with a foreign agent and that the allegations against him remain sealed.
They called for his release, arguing that interviewing controversial political figures is a fundamental part of journalism.

articles.title_orig: Air Algerie Business Class Airbus A330neo Review: Utterly Awful
articles.title_zh: Air Algerie Business Class Airbus A330neo Review: Utterly Awful
articles.content_orig:
For the first long haul segment of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip , I flew Air Algerie’s Airbus A330-900neo business class on the 6hr50min flight from Montreal (YUL) to Algiers (ALG). I had heard almost entirely negative things about Air Algerie, which intrigued me, naturally! Well, now that I’ve flown Air Algerie I can confirm that everything I heard was true, and then some.
I don’t want to be dramatic — obviously flying business class is better than economy — but honestly, just about everything sucked. On the plus side, the seats as such were fine, but that’s where the good news ends. The food was not good, and took an insanely long amount of time to be served. There were no amenity kits… or menus… or meal choice… or alcohol… or diet soda. If the crew were any more indifferent, they would’ve been invisible.
I wouldn’t fly Air Algerie again unless I absolutely had to, which… I can’t imagine that’ll ever be the case. Honestly, Air Algerie made me yearn for my recent flight on Turkmenistan Airlines , which was at least fun.
Air Algerie is a pretty isolated airline, which perhaps reflects Algeria overall — the country just isn’t interested in visitors, and getting a visa requires jumping through hoops.
So Air Algerie doesn’t have any useful partnerships when it comes to earning or redeeming miles. As a result, booking a cash ticket is just about the only option, unless you’re a frequent flyer with the airline. Air Algerie tends to have rather steep business class fares, despite its lackluster product.
However, I did manage to find a rather attractive one-way business class fare. I booked the following in business class for $1,171 in cash:
10/03 AH2701 Montreal to Algiers departing 4:10PM arriving 5:00AM (+1 day) 10/04 AH4000 Algiers to Tunis departing 7:10AM arriving 8:30AM
The first segment was operated by an Airbus A330-900neo, while the second segment was operated by an Airbus A320 that was wet leased from Avion Express.
I had flown into Montreal the same day from Miami (MIA) on Air Canada Rouge, so I had an extended layover. I was at the Air Algerie check-in counter before it opened at 12:30PM, and there was already quite the queue of passengers waiting. Unsurprisingly, and as is very common for North Africa flights, people had a ton of checked bags.
It took me around 30 minutes to get checked in, since there was one counter for business class, and there were half a dozen people in front of me. At first I was asked if I had a visa for Algeria, though I explained I was in transit, which seemed to catch the check-in agent off guard. Air Algerie is clearly targeted at the local community, and doesn’t see much international connecting traffic.
Security was a breeze, and Air Algerie sends its business class passengers to the National Bank Lounge, which is the contract lounge in the international portion of the terminal. I won’t do a full review, but it was actually a pretty pleasant facility, with plenty of seating, lots of natural light, and it wasn’t very crowded.
The food selection was pretty average, with a handful of hot options, plus cheese, cold cuts, etc. There was coffee, tea, wine, beer, and soft drinks. I made the mistake of saving my hunger and thirst for onboard the Air Algerie flight!
My Air Algerie flight was departing from gate A58, with boarding scheduled for 3:10PM, a full hour before departure. I was at the gate early enough to see the inbound aircraft arrive, and goodness, what a stunner it was!
The Montreal route is primarily served by an A330neo with the registration code 7T-VLB, which is in a special livery celebrating the country’s football team. Looking at the plane was honestly the best part of the flight experience, unfortunately.
The boarding area got very full before departure, with lots of passengers in wheelchairs, and lots of crowding around the gate. Boarding ended up starting at 3:20PM, with those needing extra time, as well as business class passengers, being invited to board first.
I can’t describe how excited I was to step onboard, as I always love trying new airlines! I wasn’t fully prepared for the level of indifference shown by every part of the experience, though.
Before I get into this review, I should mention that Air Algerie has recently started taking delivery of Airbus A330-900neos as part of its fleet modernization initiative. However, the airline isn’t just taking delivery of these planes factory fresh, but has also acquired a couple secondhand from Air Belgium, which went out of business in 2024 .
Air Algerie maintained the Air Belgium interiors — they also have staggered seats, but it’s a slightly different configuration. I boarded through the second door on the left, and then turned left into the business class cabin.
Business class takes up the entire space between the first and second set of doors, and consists of 30 seats, spread across eight rows, in a 1-2-1 configuration. These seats are from the Stelia Aerospace Solstys line, so they’re typical last generation staggered business class seats. When it comes to the seat details, they have 44″ of pitch, 21″ of width, and convert into 77″ flat beds.
On the plus side, it’s really easy to photograph Air Algerie cabins, since crews are nowhere to be seen. 😉
If you’re traveling with someone, you may appreciate the sets of center seats in odd numbered rows, as these are “honeymoon” seats, which allow you to sit really close to your companion. Meanwhile in even numbered rows, the seats in the center section are further from one another and really close to the aisles, so those would be my least preferred seats in this configuration.
Along the windows, seats alternate between being closer to the aisle and closer to the windows. In odd numbered rows, seats are closer to the aisle. What I particularly don’t like about these staggered seats is just how exposed some of them are to the aisle, as you really have no separation.
In even numbered rows, seats are closer to the windows, and these are the best seats in the house, in terms of offering some separation from the aisle, and an easy view out the window.
I assigned myself seat 6A, the window seat on the left side in the third to last row.
These staggered seats have a console to the side of the seat, and on the side of that is a panel with seat controls, an entertainment controller, and a small armrest.
There’s an exposed storage area above the panel, where you can store things, or even hang the headphones. As you can see, the seat just wasn’t well maintained, and also wasn’t clean, as it also needed a good wiping down.
In terms of charging, the AC power outlet and USB-A outlet were located underneath the seat. There was no USB-C or wireless charging, unsurprisingly.
Looking at the front of the seat, the tray table is stored behind the seat in front, and can be extended by being lowered and then moved over. One of the nice things about these tray tables is that you can angle them away from you, so it’s possible to get up during the meal service.
The entertainment system is in a fixed position and is located above the ottoman. The monitor here was 16″ and was touchscreen, but wasn’t terribly high definition.
As much as there are many aspects of this seat I don’t love, I do like how big the footwell is, which is great for those of us with big feet. It’s not necessarily that comfortable when you’re laying sideways in terms of space for knees, but still, there was a great amount of space here.
One other interesting note is that there were no overhead bins in the center of the cabin, so the overhead bins along the windows got pretty full, since the A330neo doesn’t have huge bins. On top of that, there were no individual air nozzles above seats, sadly. That was a problem on this flight, given how warm the cabin was kept.
All-in-all, Air Algerie’s business class hard product is okay. The cabin maintenance could definitely use some help, but honestly, this is the least of Air Algerie’s problems.
The Air Al

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Aramco building in Riyadh is damaged, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.
Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike.
Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike.
The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles.
The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months.
It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people , including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen.
Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group.
Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war.
An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there.
Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

articles.title_orig: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war
articles.title_zh: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war
articles.content_orig:
Iran proxy attacks target a key Saudi Arabian oil pipeline as host Kayleigh McEnany reports on the expanding conflict. Former Navy SEAL Jack Carr joins the program to discuss ballistic missile production and Chinese satellite intelligence linked to a strike killing three American troops. Carr warns that Houthis threaten global shipping chokepoints near the Red Sea.
Iran lifted its self-imposed ballistic missile-range limit and threatened to unleash new, homegrown weapons that would "astonish the entire world," within hours of the U.S. military launching a new task force aimed at choking off Tehran's weapons shipments and illicit trade Nov. 7.
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi confirmed that Iran was now abandoning its previous 2,000-kilometer, or roughly 1,240-mile, ballistic missile-range restriction, according to The Associated Press .
"That restriction has been lifted for us," Mohebbi clarified in the wake of the task force announcement.
RUSSIA SECRETLY BOLSTERED IRAN'S MISSILE ARSENAL BEFORE WAR WITH US, RECORDS UNCOVER
FILE PHOTO: Iranian missiles are displayed at the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Aerospace Force Museum in Tehran, Iran, November 15, 2024. Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia press Agency) via REUTERS
U.S. Central Command established "Task Force Iron Gate", an initiative targeting the movement of advanced Iranian weapons systems, dual-use materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
"Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with US Interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, said in a statement shared on X.
According to Behnam Taleblu, senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies ( FDD ), the U.S. may now carry out "targeted strikes" against facilitators while putting "political pressure on bordering states, as well as market and sanctions pressure against institutions underwriting Iran’s illicit trade."
"It speaks volumes, of course, that this effort is being stood up within CENTCOM headquarters," Taleblu told Fox News Digital.
Meanwhile, Iran's IRGC quickly dismissed the new initiative as "wordplay," claiming Tehran had already made preparations and coordinated with neighboring countries to withstand additional pressure, Fars News Agency reported.
Mohebbi also warned that Iran was developing new weapons capable of delivering devastating blows in another confrontation with the U.S. and Israel .
IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS
An Iranian missile is launched during a military exercise in an undisclosed location in Iran, August 20, 2025. (Iranian Army/WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Handout via REUTERS)
"There are surprises that will be unveiled and deployed on the battlefield if a third wave of confrontation with the enemy erupts. These surprises will astonish the entire world," Mohebbi said during a news conference in Tehran on Saturday, according to Iran's state-run Islamic Republic News Agency ( IRNA ).
"If they once again miscalculate, or if the Zionists, in pursuit of their own interests, lead the criminal United States into another miscalculation, they should know that Iran's next blows will be even harder and will leave them crippled for years to come," he added.
Iran's previous 2,000-kilometer limit already placed the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant, most of Egypt and parts of Greece and the Balkans within range.
In March, Iran unsuccessfully attempted to strike the joint U.S.-British military base on Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, roughly 2,500 miles from the Islamic Republic.
Mohebbi also claimed Iran was preparing to unveil new underground missile facilities, as Tehran seeks to shield its weapons production from future attacks.
The installations, described by Iranian officials as "missile cities," are designed to allow the IRGC to continue manufacturing weapons during wartime, according to IRNA.
TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS
Diego Garcia, the largest island in the Chagos archipelago and site of a major United States military base in the middle of the Indian Ocean leased from the U.K. in 1966. (reuters)
The IRGC spokesman claimed Iran's Aerospace Force continued producing missiles and drones during recent fighting, using domestic expertise without importing foreign weapons or relying on "reverse engineering of weapons captured from the enemy."
Mohebbi also described Iran's growing self-sufficiency in weapons production as a "very big achievement."
Taleblu meanwhile emphasized the significance of the Caspian Sea basin, saying the world’s largest lake has "turned into a two-way sanctions-busting hub for both Iran and Russia."
"Iranian officials always claim self-sufficiency in their military industries," he said.
"But with domestic missile production significantly constrained due to the 40-Day War, the regime will be reliant on imports to build back, and especially at scale and at a faster rate.
"This is why efforts to constrain both land and sea trade in and out of Iran are a one-two punch for the regime."
The warnings come as Washington intensified pressure on Iran's regional trade routes , including its land crossings with Iraq , where Baghdad has reportedly resisted U.S. demands for full and broader border restrictions.
According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Iraq has closed only one border crossing with Iran so far, despite reported American pressure to shut down most crossings between the two countries.
FRESH ACTIVITY EMERGES AT IRAN’S DEEPLY BURIED NUCLEAR SITE AS TRUMP WARNS IRAN NOT TO ‘GET CUTE’
Soldiers from the US-led coalition forces are seen during the handover of the K1 Air Base to the Iraqi Army from the US-led coalition in Kirkuk, Iraq on March 29, 2020. (Associated Press)
On Sunday, the U.S. Treasury pressed Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except for two as part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said, according to Reuters .
The Iraqi government had closed the al-Shayeb crossing in southeastern Iraq on Oct. 21, to review security and install equipment to prevent smuggling of prohibited materials.
Iraqi political sources told Agence France-Presse that Washington had pressured Baghdad to close most Iran-Iraq border crossings to restrict trade and financial exchanges that could help Tehran withstand U.S. sanctions, ISW reported.
ISW also said that Iranian Ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh was pressuring tribal leaders in Iraq's Maysan province to push Iraqi officials and leaders of the Shiite Coordination Framework to reopen al-Shayeb.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Al-Sadegh is reportedly a member of the IRGC's Quds Force, which oversees the organization's foreign operations.
The institute assessed that Baghdad's limited response likely reflects efforts to balance its relationship with Washington against the influence of Iranian-backed political factions.
Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title_orig: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125
articles.title_zh: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125
articles.content_orig:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo
Seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said he saw about 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to hospital. He said some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and died.
Egypt’s president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, said in a social media post that he had ordered a prompt investigation.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian railway authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Egypt’s deadliest train crash was in 2002 when more than 300 people were killed after a fire broke out on an overnight train journeying from Cairo to southern Egypt.

articles.title_orig: Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here
articles.title_zh: Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here
articles.content_orig:
SYNTH ANATOMY uses affiliation & partner programs (big red buttons) to finance a part of the activity. If you use these, you support the website. Thanks! Reading Time: 3 minutes
The Akai MPC is moving toward an open platform, and the first step is here with a GitHub repository and insights into the hardware used in the standalone MPCs.
On October 28 , Akai announced it is making its MPC Sample hardware sampler open source—as is the upcoming SampleKey . This sparked a great deal of discussion. I believe it’s actually the biggest one this year.
Then, last Friday, news broke that Akai plans to unveil 22 new products at NAMM 2027 , many of them open to experiment with. Today, Akai or inMusic has taken its first step to open its MPC platform for creators – and it’s not just the MPC Sample
Akai hasn’t made an official announcement yet, but inMusic has opened an official GitHub repository managed by Pete Goodliffe, CTO (Chief Technical Officer) and lead developer of the MPC platform. Bang, it happened, or?!
It contains the open-source components required by the licenses under which they are distributed. It does not, however, mean that inMusic or Akai has published the MPC OS as open source. This could help developers understand the underlying software environment.
Interestingly, this new repository suggests they are about to open not just the MPC Sample, but the entire MPC lineup . Plus, they’ll add the SampleKey when it is released.
Thanks for your interest in the open source software used by inMusic Brands. We are happy to comply with the requirements of the open source libraries and projects in use in our products.
This repo contains archives of the open source code for the Linux environment in our products. You will find very few changes against the upstream projects here; we aim to submit all relevant patches back up to the mainstream projects.
You can now find three different Akai MPC open releases on GitHub:
With this upcoming move, the long-running “Hakai OS” project —for example, which enables jailbreaking the MPC hardware—doesn’t go underground; it becomes an official project.
The first step in opening Pandora’s box has been taken, and a new era for the MPCs is about to start.  A game-changer, as you might say. The first step has been taken; the others will probably follow soon.
We will soon see numerous new projects that will transform the hardware, both the standalones and MPC Sample, into entirely new instruments.  If the community embraces this, inMusic’s plan will have succeeded.
As they communicated yesterday, they want to give creators hardware for making music and also to experiment with their own crafted or AI-generated tools. We have some exciting months ahead, during which it remains to be seen what exactly will come our way.
The Akai MPC framework and its components are now open source and available on GitHub.
More information here: Akai Pro / GitHub
Available from my partners
WaveTracker is a free and open-source wave-based chiptune tracker software powered by wavetable synthesis and sampling. In recent years, trackers have made a comeback in hardware form. See the XOR NerdSEQ module, the Polyend Tracker, […]
Xenos is a new free Synthesizer plugin (Raphael Radna) using a novel dynamic stochastic synthesis (DSS) that makes wild sounds possible. The core of every Synthesizer plugin, whether free or commercial, uses one or multiple […]
Great news coming from the AudioKit Pro developers. AudioKit Synth One, a great sounding, open source Synthesizer is available now for iPhone. What you get here for free is amazing: it sounds great, has a lot […]
Sweet! No more paying for basic features like the clip launcher. 🙂
We aren’t quite there yet. For now, the MPC framework and components—the foundation for the MPC OS—are free and open for custom operating systems.
What do you mean that the OS is not open? I don’t understand the difference 😅😅 Does it mean that user OS can be installed, but the original OS can’t be changed? But then you said that unofficial plugins can be used, which I assume involves the original OS 😵‍💫😵‍💫
The MPCs are based on a Linux foundation with added components, such as the controls. So, the “bed” on which the MPC OS lies. This is now open and people can make their own OS on this base. The MPC OS, the operation system, isn’t open-source yet and not if it will be. We will see this
Akai’s “open source” release is not what many people think it is
Akai has published source code for the MPC G1 line (MPC Live II, One, X, Force and others), and the first reaction I saw was: “Great, now we can write our own synths for the MPC.” I don’t think that’s what this is.
I went through the repository. It’s a license-compliance archive, the kind a company has to publish when its devices ship GPL and LGPL software. It holds 72 source packages: a custom Linux kernel, systemd, ALSA, busybox and similar parts. It doesn’t contain the MPC application, the plugin host, the AIR instruments or any SDK.
I also looked into the MPC 3 desktop software installed on my machine. Its bundled plugins are only skins and presets. The sound engines are compiled into the app. It does contain an embedded Lua engine, but it looks like an internal automation tool for reading and comparing UI state, not a scripting feature for users. I found no way to load your own scripts. That’s my reading of the files, not a statement from Akai.
Akai’s own support page also says third-party plugins can’t be loaded in standalone mode.
So what does the release give us? A look at the Linux foundation under the hardware, which is useful for researchers. Custom synths on a Live II it does not give us. If that changes, it will need an official plugin format from Akai.
I use an MPC Live II as part of my dawless rig, so I’d love to be wrong about this.
Exactly what I wrote: the MPC OS isn’t open-source, but the foundation it sits on is. So the bed on which people can code/vibe-code their own custom OS. I’m not sure if Akai will open-source the O.
So why use such a clickbaity title then? Oh right, because that’s what we do in marketing these days.
The framework and its components are open source! You can create your own custom firmware for it. So the MPC hardware is open source.
The title isn’t misleading or clickbait because it says “Akai MPC is now open-source”. It doesn’t say “Akai MPC OS is now open-source”.
Ok, let me try again. Yes, you didn’t write “Akai MPC OS is now open-source”. However, in the current trend of people modding firmware, and companies picking up to the trend of open sourcing their whole firmware (including actual features like sampler and reverbs etc.), this is what a typical user would kind of expect when the title says “Akai MPC is now open-source”.
We must return to reading actual articles instead of just titles so they understand what it is actually about.
So what is so good about it?
I had a look through the Gen 2 files. They’re mostly the standard Linux parts Akai has to publish to stay compliant with open-source licenses (kernel, bootloader, system libraries), not the MPC software itself. Still useful for tinkerers, but it doesn’t unlock anything or add plugin support on its own.
I believe this is just the required source disclosures from open source components they use, not the intended framework for anyone to make their own software / run additional things on the devices. This doesn’t, for instance, compile or run on devices without AKAI’s signing keys.
It is a great step and gives some nice disclosure as to the hardware layout, but I think you may have jumped the gun a bit on this one.
I made it clearer, and as usual with my articles, I’ll update and extend them with new information as it becomes available. This is the first step in the new “open” era of the MPC.
Yup, hopefully more steps soon!
Open platform, not open source.  Big difference and honestly much better option.
so they published the open source libraries they used on their machines? that’s r

Sequoia Capital announced some major changes this week, including the closure of its London office, the merger of its early-stage and growth teams, and the end of its Scouts program .
Now, the Financial Times has published a report painting all of this as an attempt to undo the legacy of former leader Roelof Botha, who stepped down as the firm’s steward last year . An unnamed source told the FT that Botha “loved process and hierarchy,” while “the rest of the team didn’t.”
Apparently, not everyone is on-board with the changes, with another source firing back that this seems like an “erasure of Sequoia’s heritage, not Roelof’s legacy.”

A Sequoia spokesperson said that the firm continues to “collaborate closely” with Botha.

articles.title_orig: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
articles.title_zh: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
articles.content_orig:
A view through the destroyed walls of a kindergarten shows a large bomb crater and a damaged residential apartment building following a missile attack in Kyiv, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption
European officials will turn up for the U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates this week, France's foreign minister said Sunday, days after the Kremlin had insisted there could be no role for European powers at the meeting.
"France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio. He did not say who would represent Paris, or whether French or other European officials would take part directly in negotiations, or simply observe.
The meetings, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, had previously been presented as a three-way session between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.
Talking to a Russian news channel on Friday, he accused European governments of failing to decide who speaks for them, while acknowledging that security talks would at some point require Europe's involvement.
On Thursday, President Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and said a coming agreement was "going to involve more than Ukraine," adding he could even say it "might involve all of Europe."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN on Friday that he had not been given details of the agreement Trump had referenced, and warned: "For me, it's not simple, and it can be dangerous." He invoked the 1945 Yalta conference, where Allied leaders settled Europe's division without the involvement of several affected countries.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attend a press conference in Berlin, Germany, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ebrahim Noroozi/AP hide caption
This will be the fourth round of talks between the two warring nations brokered by the Trump administration, and the first since those in Geneva this February. Earlier U.S.-brokered meetings have made little progress, and the chances of a breakthrough have been reduced as the Trump administration focused on its war with Iran.
Moscow confirmed it would return to the negotiating table only following a visit by U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in October. Those talks saw Putin announce the release of an American prisoner from a Russian jail — an apparent Kremlin gesture to President Trump's earlier lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Ukraine was vehemently opposed to the fuel sales — arguing they helped replenish Moscow's war chest.
Witkoff has said the agenda for these latest talks will include postwar security arrangements and de-escalation of the conflict and humanitarian issues, shortly after Melania Trump helped broker a limited ceasefire that allowed humanitarian aid to enter a town inside Russian-occupied Ukraine.
Russia's delegation will again be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline Putin aide who has participated in most talks with Ukraine since the unsuccessful first set of discussions all the way back in March 2022.
For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky, a deputy head of the General Staff's operations directorate, alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.
This more senior lineup could indicate that Moscow is readier than before to address thorny political and military questions. But the U.S. think tankInstitute for the Study of War suggested some of those same Russian officials have in fact previously sought to slow down previous talks or push harder on Moscow's demands.
The gaps between the two countries remain substantial. Russia has demanded that Ukraine give up large parts of its territory and renounce NATO membership. Zelenskyy has repeatedly insisted any security commitments should be clearly spelled out, including who would act, and how, if Russia attacked again.
Russian President Vladimir Putin, right, interacts with people at the monument to merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky, leaders of the struggle against foreign invaders in 1612, in Red Square in Moscow, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, during National Unity Day celebrations. Yuri Kochetkov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
Some analysts expect little. In an op-ed for the Atlantic Council think tank, the former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst argued that Putin had rejected every U.S. proposal Kyiv accepted and preferred participating in peace talks than pursuing actual peace. "Perhaps the only outcome of the talks," he wrote, "will be to agree to another round."
The meetings in the United Arab Emirates also follow Democrats' midterm victories, which Zelenskyy said could improve Ukraine's chances of more U.S. aid.
Russia, too, may be looking to push for the Trump administration's outlines of a Ukraine deal — before a Democratic-controlled Congress arrives come January.
Also hovering over the talks — the prospect of Trump, Xi, and Putin gathering for a trilateral meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China later this month. While details remain murky, all sides have confirmed discussions are underway.
And as officials travel to Abu Dhabi to talk peace, the war has raged on regardless.
Zelenskyy said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area overnight Saturday, with only four intercepted, accusing Moscow of treating diplomacy "as a form of aggression."
In southern Ukraine, the death toll from a guided-bomb strike Monday on an aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha rose to at least 55.

articles.title_orig: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.title_zh: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.content_orig:
The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) is considering a major restructuring that could see thousands of its employees laid off and some of its responsibilities transferred to other bodies, including US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, according to multiple media reports citing diplomatic sources.
The reported proposal is spearheaded by UNRWA’s acting commissioner-general, Christian Saunders, and comes as the agency faces a severe financial crisis.
Trump’s Board of Peace (BoP), established under the framework endorsed by the UN Security Council in November 2025, is tasked with overseeing Gaza’s transitional governance, reconstruction, economic recovery, and coordination of humanitarian assistance.
The BoP has been explicit in its opposition to the UN agency set up for Palestinian refugees only, making it clear in a July 1 statement that “UNRWA has no place in the new Gaza .”
“We are turning the page on the complex of perpetual aid dependency and conflict. The people of Gaza deserve better,” the BoP said in a social media post on September 25.
In the same post, the BoP said it would “only work with trusted partners who will deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a de-radicalized Strip. UNRWA fails on those litmus tests.”
However, the Associated Press reported, also on September 25, that BoP representatives have held several private meetings with UNRWA officials. A BoP official acknowledged that some of the agency’s programs and vetted employees could continue if they were effective and accountable, while maintaining that the UN body’s institutional role was ending.
UN Watch’s Hillel Neuer posted last week that there is a plan to unravel UNRWA, which has long faced criticism from Israel, the United States, and UN Watch over allegations of links between some of its employees and terrorist organizations such as Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) – including participating in October 7 and holding hostages.
According to Israel Hayom , which cited Arab and Western diplomatic sources, discussions have taken place about transferring some of UNRWA’s responsibilities to the BoP and other bodies.
Some of the agency’s remit could reportedly also be transferred to the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the West Bank.
The reported proposal was presented by Saunders at a meeting of UNRWA’s Advisory Commission, with the agency’s financial difficulties cited as a central reason for the restructuring. Saunders told Anadolu Agency on October 20 that the agency’s deficit stood at approximately $70 million.
“If we don’t receive money in the very near future, I will have to take some regrettable actions in order to ensure that we’re able to finish the year and to pay our staff salaries,” Saunders warned.
The head of the Arab Staff Union in Gaza, Mustafa Al-Ghoul, told the Mondoweiss anti-Zionist news site last week that UNRWA had dismissed around 1,000 staff in Gaza and let 2,000 retire without replacing them, leaving roughly 10,500.
Saunders gave the same figures in the Anadolu Agency interview, saying “We have 10,500 personnel on the ground [in the Gaza Strip].”
He also expressed support for the broader international framework for Gaza, saying: “ US President Trump ’s 20-point plan, UN Security Council Resolution 2803, the Board of Peace, and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza – we are completely behind these efforts.”
Separately, Swiss French-language daily newspaper Le Temps published an investigation last week saying that Saunders plans for UNRWA to close its doors “within four or five years.” This has not yet been independently verified.
Under the UN-backed framework, the BoP is to exercise transitional authority in Gaza until the PA has completed its reform program and can securely and effectively resume control. In the meantime, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is intended to serve as an interim technocratic administration.
Currently, UNRWA purports to be assisting more than 1.7 million Palestinians in Gaza, providing healthcare through 11 centers, schooling for approximately 300,000 children, and drinking water for around 820,000 people.
It also says it provides essential services to nearly six million Palestinian refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, and the West Bank.
