articles.title_orig: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.title_zh: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.content_orig:
By ROB HULL, MOTORING EDITOR
Updated: 13:34 EDT, 8 November 2026
We've had the Temu Range Rover; now there's an AliExpress Roller.
Chinese brand Yangwang, a spin-off from electric car giant BYD, has unveiled a new battery-powered luxury vehicle called the Altior, and it bears a striking resemblance to the iconic British Rolls-Royce Phantom limousine – but for around half the price.
At 5.6m long, with a vast bonnet and grille, rear-hinged coach doors, a palatial interior and umbrellas stowed inside the door panels, there's no hiding which ostentatious motor it has firmly set its sights on.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, with the car 'expressing an ambition to elevate the experience of luxury through cultural depth, personal expression and technological progress', Yangwang says.
Just 399 are going to be produced and reports in China suggest pre-orders are available from 2million yuan, which equates to around £230,000.
That puts it closer to the £250,000 Rolls-Royce Ghost than the flagship £450,000 Phantom, though that's before taking into account heavily subsidised pricing in China's domestic market.
Its global premiere in Abu Dhabi this weekend comes just days after car registration figures revealed that Jaecoo's 'Temu Range Rover' 7 SUV was the UK's best-selling new model for a second successive month .
The runaway success of the Range Rover Velar lookalike is the clearest sign yet that Chinese brands are coming for the old guard of established luxury carmakers. And with the Altior, it appears not even Rolls-Royce is safe.
This is the new Yangwang Altior limousine - a luxury Rolls-Royce Phantom rival from Chinese EV giant, BYD
While the Rolls-Royce Phantom and Ghost feature a gutsy 6.75-litre twin-turbocharged V12 petrol engine, the Yangwang Altior is a far greener proposition.
It uses a version of the quad-electric motor setup deployed in the Chinese firm's other models, the U8 SUV and U9 supercar. That's likely to produce more than 1,000bhp and will allow it to perform a tank turn , rotating each wheel independently to spin the vehicle on its own axis.
Providing the energy for the e-motors is BYD's second-generation Blade Battery technology.
As such, it's claimed to be capable of travelling more than 621 miles on a full charge. However, this is based on Chinese efficiency tests that are historically a shade more optimistic than Europe's cycle, which would be closer to 520 miles.
The battery is compatible with BYD's network of Flash Charging stations, of which there are 10,000 already in China and a promise to install 300 here in the UK .
The ground-breaking devices can deliver up to 1,500kW of power and top up a battery pack from 10 to 70 per cent charge in as little as five minutes, before reaching full charge in less than ten.
That's not all in terms of technological advances.
The Yangwang boasts a suite of chassis tech that means it can float if there are flash floods or the driver 'accidentally enters water'. And it can continue tracking in a straight line when one of the tyres suffers a high-speed blowout on the motorway.
The Altior also taps into BYD's God's Eye A assisted-driving system, which includes parking-space-to-parking-space navigation assistance. This enables the car to drive itself from one car park to another, even when they are hundreds of miles apart.
The suspension is clever too. The brand's DiSus active body control system uses cameras to read the road ahead and adjusts damping in real time, meaning occupants won't feel potholes or changes in road surfaces while stretched out in the back.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, as BYD's spin-off Yangwang looks to enter a more opulent market with its latest model. And it certain strikes a resemblance to the Rolls-Royce Phantom
Squint slightly and there's no mistaking the Rolls-Royce-inspired silhouette.
The elongated bonnet, despite there being no 12-cylinder combustion engine lurking beneath it, and the glitzy upright grille are trademarks of the 122-year-old British marque.
The Altior's front end is described as a 'masterpiece of high jewellery'.
'Meticulous selection, polishing and individual placement create a composition that responds to changing light, revealing new depth and brilliance as the viewpoint moves,' the Chinese manufacturer says.
Its lights are a little special too, featuring 12 individual elements that rotate from the outside to the centre to create a 'ceremonial welcome' when the owner approaches.
At 5.6m long, the Altior (pictured left) is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom (pictured right)
Like all Roller limousines, the Chinese Yangwang has rear-hinged coach doors
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom
Is it time for European luxury car makers to fear China’s fast-rising electric rivals?
At 5.6m long, the Altior is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom.
However, the Yangwang's other dimensions, including a width of 2m, a height of almost 1.6m and a wheelbase of 3.5m, are almost like-for-like with the bigger of the two Rolls-Royces.
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom.
The doors also open in the fashion for which Rolls-Royce is famed, providing generous access to the opulent interior.
The finely crafted bespoke umbrellas hidden in each door panel, much like those in a Rolls-Royce, are said to be inspired by the circular wooden roof of the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at China's Temple of Heaven complex.
The cockpit is the least Roller-like part of the car. While the British luxury firm attempts to conceal tech for a traditional look, the Yangwang has a dashboard-wide high-definition screen
Exactly like Rolls-Royces, though, the Chinese limo has bespoke, hand-crafted umbrellas hidden in a compartment within the doors
Step inside and the cabin – dubbed a 'private lounge' – is awash with only the highest-quality materials.
These include hammer-tested metal switches, pure-wool floor mats, real-wood veneers, 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons and semi-aniline leather upholstery.
The designers have even mounted polished yellow jade gemstones inside the vertical air vents, while the silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs.
The cockpit itself looks a little less Rolls-Royce-esque, even if it does feature a chrome-rimmed steering wheel wrapped in beautifully finished leather.
While the British car maker generally tries to subtly conceal much of its modern technology up front, the Yangwang has a dashboard-spanning digital glass display. This incorporates an instrument cluster with classic-style digital dials and an enormous infotainment screen featuring a laptop-style taskbar of icons.
But it's the rear compartment that well-heeled customers will want to know about.
The cabin is as palatial as you'd expect from a Rolls-Royce or Bentley limo. It boasts aviation-style zero-gravity seats, real-wood veneers and 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons
There's a fridge in the rear and in the front, two champagne flute holders and a control panel that means you won't have to converse with your chauffeur at all
There's plenty of artistry too. Silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs
The four-seat layout is almost perfectly symmetrical and 'gives each occupant a clearly defined personal space' where the owner in the back can feel entirely separate from Jeeves behind the wheel by elevating a divider between them.
Owners won't need to ask their chauffeur for anything, either.
Rear occupants can access all key functions through the central console, including lowering the front passenger seat at the touch of a button to provide an uninterrupted view ahead.
The rear chairs are 'aviation-style zero-gravity seats' that provide a 'deeply relaxed'

articles.title_orig: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Found in Smugglers’ Socks at Peru Airport
articles.title_zh: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Found in Smugglers’ Socks at Peru Airport
articles.content_orig:
Three suitcases’ worth of the spiders were on their way to Germany, where they could fetch an estimated €1.5m
More than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to Germany, Peruvian authorities said.
The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agence France-Presse on Thursday.
They were spotted after agents noticed some unusual wriggling inside the luggage during a routine customs inspection at Jorge Chávez international airport. “We noticed that some of them were moving. There were small ones and large ones,” said Cora Suarez, a SERFOR wildlife control technician.
One tarantula can sell for about €500 ($560) in Europe, Suarez said, meaning the wildlife trafficking scheme would be potentially worth €1.5m for just one trip.
The hidden arachnids, which came from several regions of Peru, were found in varying stages of development, from eggs and hatchlings to adults, Suarez said.
The Europeans accused of smuggling the tarantulas were detained by police specialising in environmental crimes and will face criminal proceedings, SERFOR said.
Illegal wildlife trafficking is a highly lucrative criminal activity that generates around $20bn annually worldwide, according to Interpol.
Such trafficking is among the primary causes of the loss of biodiversity on the planet.

articles.title_orig: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.title_zh: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump / Alex Brandon / Pool via AP Photo
President Donald Trump said Sunday that a renewed war with Iran is “highly unlikely” if Tehran makes progress toward a nuclear agreement and reopens the Strait of Hormuz — while warning that the U.S. has 38 Iranian bridges in its sights.
“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN .
Trump said military action would probably not be necessary, but warned that the U.S. is prepared to strike Iran again.
“The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary,” Trump said. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301% inflation. Highly unlikely it will be necessary. I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them.”
Trump added that it is “highly unlikely” he would have to order another attack.
“They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off,” he warned.
“We’re ready for it. I’ve got three aircraft carriers here. The other one just arrived. We have three. They’re fully locked and loaded,” Trump continued.
He also said the U.S. could destroy dozens of bridges in Iran within hours.
“We have 38 bridges in our sight that we can knock down in literally one hour,” Trump said. “They’ll all be down.”
“I don’t want to do that because, essentially, it’ll take 10 years to rebuild them,” he added. “I don’t like ripping down bridges. And the hardest thing to build is a bridge. It takes years, and I’m a good builder.”
Diplomatic activity across the Middle East has continued since Thursday, with Qatar mediating efforts to advance talks between Washington and Tehran
Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized Iran's conditions for ending the war Sunday, warning that efforts to secure a diplomatic agreement with Tehran have yielded little progress.
"You have a number of countries that continue to engage them with different ideas," Rubio told reporters while traveling to a G7 meeting in Paris.
"But I wouldn't say we're at the verge of a breakthrough," he said.
Rubio emphasized that President Donald Trump remains committed to pursuing a diplomatic solution, even as negotiations face significant obstacles.
"The president would always prefer to solve this and every problem diplomatically," Rubio said.
"Sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately, but if there's a chance to do it we'll explore it," he added.
"Right now, it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic," he said.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump's actions against Iran on Sunday, arguing he confronted a national security threat that previous presidents failed to address.
“The president of the United States identified a very real threat to this country that's existed for a very long period of time,” Rubio told reporters before departing for Paris for the G7 meeting.
“So I think the president took on something that other presidents have failed to do,” he added.
“There needs to be bipartisan acknowledgment that a nuclear Iran would be completely unacceptable and dangerous for the United States, not just Israel, not just the Middle East, the whole world and the United States,” Rubio said.
Rubio also defended Washington's right to protect U.S. forces and shipping in the region against potential threats.
“We have a right to defend ourselves,” Rubio said.
Yemen's armed forces said Sunday they carried out nearly 1,000 strikes, including dozens of air and drone attacks, in a major offensive that reportedly left hundreds of militia fighters dead, wounded or on the run.
Brig. Gen. Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaili, a spokesman for Yemen's armed forces, announced the operations Sunday in a post on X .
The forces said they carried out 19 airstrikes on the Marib, Taiz and Tur al-Bahah fronts, targeting militia positions, troop concentrations and vehicles. Drones conducted another 29 strikes on combat positions, vehicles, weapons and other militia assets.
“Field artillery and rocket launchers also carried out 944 strikes on militia concentrations and reinforcements, firing positions, fortifications, barricades, and sniper positions,” Al-Nuzaili added.
The strikes killed, wounded or forced approximately 267 militia commanders and fighters to flee the battlefield, according to the statement. The attacks also destroyed or damaged 97 military vehicles.
Yemen's army also released footage of a Houthi ambush carried out by troops it described as “the heroes of the 1st Emergency Division forces.”
President Donald Trump / Getty Images
President Donald Trump on Sunday touted Washington’s new U.S. military task force aimed at choking off Iran's weapons supply routes, as it ramps up pressure through its maritime blockade.
“Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect in the Islamic Republic of Iran ,” Trump said on Truth Social.
“Coupled with history’s greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!” he added.
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the formation of Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday, saying the roughly 20-person team will be based in Tampa, Florida, and work to disrupt the movement of weapons, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein / Khalil Dawood / Xinhua via Getty Images
The U.S. Treasury Department asked that Iraq shut down all but two of its border crossings with Iran as part of a drive to isolate Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Sunday, according to Reuters .
“There are many official and unofficial border crossings with Iran, and closing all of them would be difficult and would affect our economy.
“The Americans are still demanding the closure of the crossings, and we are currently in discussions with them,” Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera.
The development came as U.S. Central Command ( CENTCOM ) moved to close off Tehran’s overland corridors militarily, directing the establishment of Task Force Iron Gate on Nov. 7.
Adm. Brad Cooper said the initiative was to build on the “success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea” and would “further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military.”
Iran's foreign minister issued a stark ultimatum to the White House on Sunday, warning that Tehran's forces would "rain down hell" if Washington chooses war over a diplomatic proposal aimed at ending the war.
“American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own,” Abbas Araghchi said of the latest proposal sent to Washington.
“Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results,” he said on X .
“Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell,” he warned.
According to Reuters , Araghchi also said Sunday that the midterm results had temporarily stalled mediation efforts aimed at securing a deal between Tehran and Washington.
Araghchi told Iranian state television that Tehran would have to wait for mediators to resume diplomatic efforts.
Iran submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar on Thursday, a senior Iranian official told Reuters.

articles.title_orig: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.title_zh: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.
On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.
That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".
Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.
And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.
The Prince of Wales and the Princess Royal were among royals in attendance, along with military chiefs, senior politicians, diplomats and faith leaders, watched by big crowds squeezed behind railings along Whitehall.
Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales watched from a balcony above the Cenotaph in the Foreign Office.
Among the flags on the roof of that Whitehall building was the Ukrainian blue and yellow. It went up when Russia invaded and four years later it is now visibly frayed - a reminder of the length of that war and of current threats.
At 11:00 GMT, as the first strike of Big Ben echoed from the nearby Houses of Parliament, the big two-minute silence filled the usually frenetic streets, before the playing of the Last Post.
The King had his eyes closed, the crowds in Whitehall stopped for their own thoughts, in a rare moment of calm in the capital.
The poignant parade past the Cenotaph included representatives of about 340 different military and civilian groups, from the Royal Naval Association and the Royal Marines Association to Transport for London and the Royal National Lifeboat Institute.
Alongside those marching were flotillas of disability scooters and families helping veterans in wheelchairs.
Those who took part in WW2 are now increasingly frail - and there were 12 participants in the march-past compared to 20 last year. The oldest participant this year was aged 105.
Taking part for the first time was 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who had been part of the Land Army that had helped to feed the country at war.
She had joined the Land Army in 1940 as a 16-year-old, having lied about her age, and worked on a farm in Leicestershire.
"I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I'm very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don't quite know what to expect," she said.
"I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn't return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the annual event was a time to "reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others".
He earlier announced that he wanted to tackle the problem of homelessness among ex-service personnel to "ensure that any veteran sleeping rough is offered appropriate accommodation before Christmas".
Mark Atkinson, the director general of the Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today."
Remembrance events took place across the country as thousands gathered to pay their respects to those who died in past conflicts.
First Minister of Scotland John Swinney placed a wreath at the Stone of Remembrance outside the City Chambers during an event in Edinburgh.
Veterans, military personnel and cadets also marched through the centres of British cities such as Manchester, Birmingham and Leeds.
A silent poppy drop was held as part of the Festival of Remembrance at Durham Cathedral while wreaths were laid at Canterbury Cathedral.
Separately, the Duke of Sussex was seen attending a Remembrance service in the market town of Brackley in Northamptonshire.
For more than a century, the national Remembrance event has been held around the Cenotaph.
The monument was built as a focal point for honouring those who had fought and died in World War One, including those who had no grave, and as a place to mourn for those families who might not be able to visit war cemeteries overseas.
The word "cenotaph" means "empty tomb" in Greek and it was designed by the architect Sir Edwin Lutyens in a simple, austere style, with no sense of triumphalism and with almost no decoration.
The monument had been originally built in 1919 as a temporary, plaster and wood structure. But it proved so popular with the public that it was replaced in 1920 with a permanent version, in the same design but in stone.
It was opened at 11:00 on 11 November 1920 by King George V. His great-grandson, Charles, was there again, on an overcast morning 106 years later, to continue paying respect.

articles.title_orig: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
articles.title_zh: Eisenkot open to Netanyahu joining Israel’s next government
articles.content_orig:
Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot , the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup.
In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.
“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said.
Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. At the ceremony, Eisenkot said he will act in the interests of the public and represent all parts of Israeli society.
Herzog, meanwhile, warned that the country faced uncertainties after the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, which brought victories for several political figures critical of Israel and the US’s military support.
“The State of Israel needs a stable government,” Herzog said, pointing to the “new political reality” in the US.
Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.
Despite this, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate to replace Netanyahu.
In Israel’s October 27 elections , Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.
Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.
He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.
“Netanyahu still has time to derail Gadi Eisenkot’s efforts to form a government and sabotage attempts to gain a vote of confidence,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank.
“In the meantime, he remains caretaker prime minister. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would be the natural second in line to be tasked with forming a government. And if he fails, elections would then be called, and that would still allow Netanyahu to remain as caretaker.
“Many of Netanyahu’s critics say that is his aim. The big question in Israeli politics now is: does the opposition really want to get rid of Netanyahu? Or is the opposition to Palestinian Israelis in mainstream politics so strong that they’re willing to risk keeping Netanyahu in power by going back to the ballot box?”

articles.title_orig: Ghana Cancels 10 Passports Issued Illegally After Applicants Allegedly Paid Up To $29,000, Suspends Two Officials
articles.title_zh: Ghana Cancels 10 Passports Issued Illegally After Applicants Allegedly Paid Up To $29,000, Suspends Two Officials
articles.content_orig:
According to the ministry, one petitioner claimed to have paid $29,000 in 2023, while another alleged that he paid $5,000 in 2026 to members of the suspected criminal network.
Ghana’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cancelled 10 service passports allegedly issued illegally to individuals who did not qualify for them after paying members of a suspected criminal syndicate, as part of an investigation into a passport-for-sale scheme dating back to 2023.
The ministry also announced the interdiction of two officials, including the Acting Director of Passports, Mahama Yahaya Amantana, and a junior Foreign Service Officer, Alhassan Sumani, over their alleged roles in the scheme.
In a statement issued in Accra on Sunday, November 8, 2026, the ministry said the investigation followed two petitions alleging irregularities in the issuance of service passports.
According to the ministry, one petitioner claimed to have paid $29,000 in 2023, while another alleged that he paid $5,000 in 2026 to members of the suspected criminal network.
The ministry said the first petition was received on October 8, 2026, prompting the Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to order the establishment of an investigative committee on October 13.
It said preliminary findings had confirmed that individuals who were not qualified to receive service passports obtained them after allegedly making illegal payments to a syndicate.
The 10 passports identified in the investigation were issued between January 2023 and August 2026.
Those affected include Richard Sakyi Apenteng and Augustina Agyei Boateng, whose passports were issued on January 3, 2023; Juliet Amankwa, issued on January 31, 2023; and Rebecca Agyeiwaa, issued on February 2, 2023.
Others are Prince Ahensah and Maybel Ahensah, whose passports were issued on May 28, 2026; Twumasi Francis Kwame, Gyabaah Anthony, Frederick Ennin and Bosompem Richard, whose passports were issued in August 2026.
The ministry said all 10 passports had been cancelled and could no longer be used.
It added that international partners had been notified of the cancellations, while efforts were underway to track down the beneficiaries, including two individuals who allegedly used the illegally obtained passports to travel in 2023.
The ministry identified Sumani as a key figure named in all the petitions, alleging that he operated as a passport-processing intermediary, commonly referred to as a “goro boy”, in 2023 before being recruited into the Foreign Service on November 29, 2024.
It said both Sumani and Amantana had been interdicted and referred to the Ghana Police Service for further investigations and possible prosecution.
The ministry also announced that Ambassador Mohammed Habib Idris, who served as Director of Passports during the period under investigation in 2023 and has since retired, would be investigated by security agencies.
It said he would be sanctioned if found culpable, just like the other officials under investigation.
“In the interest of fairness, impartiality and non-discrimination, the Director of Passports for the 2023 period in issue, Ambassador Mohammed Habib Idris, who is now retired, would also be investigated by the security services and sanctioned if found culpable just like his counterpart, Mr. Mahama Yahaya Amantana,” the statement said.
The ministry described the alleged operation as a sophisticated scheme that began before the current administration but said the investigation had exposed those behind it.
“It is apparent that this Service Passport For Sale Scheme was a sophisticated operation which predates the current administration, we are however glad that the masterminds have finally been exposed and rounded up due to our heightened diligence and zero tolerance for corruption,” it said.
The ministry also sought to distinguish the investigation from allegations involving diplomatic passports, insisting that there was no evidence that the country's diplomatic passports were being sold.
“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs wishes to state for the record that so far, no evidence has emerged that Ghana's Diplomatic Passports are being sold.
“For the avoidance of doubt, the matters under investigations are about Service Passports and not Diplomatic Passports,” the statement added.
The ministry said it was committed to ensuring that those responsible for the alleged irregularities were prosecuted, promising transparency and accountability throughout the investigation.
It also provided figures showing that 1,397 service passports were issued between 2009 and 2016, while 3,174 were issued between 2017 and 2024. A further 754 have been issued from 2025 to date.
For diplomatic passports, the ministry said 2,899 were issued between 2009 and 2016, 5,682 between 2017 and 2024, and 1,944 since 2025.
The statement also highlighted reforms introduced under President John Dramani Mahama, including the introduction of chip-embedded passports compliant with International Civil Aviation Organization standards, the establishment of passport application centres across all 16 regions, 24-hour operations, free courier delivery and an electronic tracking system.
It said the government had also reduced the passport application fee from GH₵500 to GH₵350 to make the document more affordable.
The ministry said the reforms were aimed at strengthening the credibility, security and efficiency of Ghana's passport administration system.

articles.title_orig: What Lies Behind russia's Decision Not to Supply Iran with the S-400 Air Defense System?
articles.title_zh: What Lies Behind russia's Decision Not to Supply Iran with the S-400 Air Defense System?
articles.content_orig:
Iran has resumed talks with russia on strengthening its air defense capabilities, with a particular focus on acquiring the S-400 missile defense system, which Tehran had previously sought to obtain. This decision was discussed during a visit to russia by Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, on November 5.
According to The Telegraph , Tehran remains hopeful about reaching such an agreement, despite U.S. President Donald Trump's claim that russia is "not helping" Iran. During the visit, Iranian officials were presented with proposals on how to prepare for a potential war with the U.S., particularly by strengthening ties with russia in the field of military-technical cooperation.
From Defense Express we would like to note that, Despite Trump's repeated attempts to downplay the extent of russian-Iranian cooperation, recent reports suggest that Moscow has agreed to supply Tehran with 90 launchers for Kh-39 LMUR air-to-ground guided missiles. This decision clearly indicates an active partnership between the two countries, especially given that the russian federation is using the aforementioned weapons in the war against Ukraine.
However, the delivery of the S-400 air defense system to Iran currently seems more like a pipe dream than a reality, and there are several reasons for this. The S-400 is russia's primary air defense system, designed to detect and destroy aerial targets, including aircraft, drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles. Given the scale of Ukrainian strikes against russian oil refineries and critical infrastructure, weakening russia's own air defense capabilities would make little sense. Moreover, the air defense systems are also becoming targets of Ukrainian strikes. in August, it was reported that Ukraine's Special Operations had struck an S-400 system in Gelendzhik.
In light of this, russia needs to ramp up production of the S-400 systems for its own needs, which also presents significant challenges. The system includes a command post, radars, launchers, missiles, and support equipment, the production of which relies heavily on foreign components, particularly microelectronics. For instance, the radar uses RO4003C high-frequency laminates from the American company Rogers Corporation, and the production of the missile's navigation module requires autonomous inertial systems with French-made laser gyroscopes.
Although russia has found ways to circumvent international sanctions, the restrictions continue to constrain and slow down the production of S-400 systems. Strikes on manufacturing facilities also threaten the continuity of S-400 production, with Ukrainian military drones repeatedly targeting facilities operated by the Almaz-Antey defense conglomerate. Moreover, the machine tools used to manufacture S-400 components are likely to rely heavily on Western-made parts and software.
It is also worth noting that russian forces are using S-400 systems to carry out ballistic missile strikes against Ukraine with RM-48U surface-to-surface missiles. Given this, it is important to distinguish between the systems used for offensive and defensive operations, as they employ different types of weaponry.
To summarize, we can mention the contract under which russia agreed to supply Turkiye with two divisional sets—four S-400 batteries. The fulfillment of the contract took 31 months, from its signing to the delivery of the components. So even if russia decides to manufacture S-400 systems for Iran from scratch, it will take quite some time.

articles.title_orig: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.title_zh: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.content_orig:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone” , in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.
The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.
The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.
The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion
In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.
Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.
The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of thousands join Amsterdam’s ‘Red Line’ protest against Israel
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of thousands join Amsterdam’s ‘Red Line’ protest against Israel
articles.content_orig:
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
At least 200,000 protesters joined the ongoing march in Amsterdam for the country’s fourth “Red Line” rally, demanding tougher action by the Dutch government against Israel’s war on Gaza. The estimated number comes from the rally’s organisers.
The Rights Forum along with 13 other groups, including Amnesty International, PAX and Oxfam Novib, set up the demonstration to demand the Dutch government stop buying Israeli weapons and impose sanctions on the country for war crimes.
Extra transport has been put in place, including more metros and longer NS trains to Amsterdam. Trams and buses around Museumplein are being diverted. The rally starts on Museumplein at 1pm with speeches, followed by a march through Amsterdam Zuid and Oud-West from 1.45pm to 4pm.
Previous Red Line rallies have drawn huge crowds. Organisers estimated turnout at more than 100,000 in The Hague in May 2025, 150,000 in The Hague in June 2025 and 250,000 in Amsterdam last October.
There has been some controversy in the run-up to the protest. Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who joined a previous Red Line protest as D66 leader, said at his weekly press conference on Friday that he would not be attending this one and that it would be inappropriate for him to do so now that he is prime minister.
Some of the speakers at the rally have also been accused of links to Hamas and other armed Palestinian groups. These include Omar Barghouti, co-founder of the BDS boycott movement, and Medhat Alamawi of the Palestinian Community Netherlands, who is also involved with activist group Utrecht4Palestine.
The Rights Forum spokesman Edwin van ’t Pad dismissed the criticism, telling newssite de Kanttekening: “Even if we had put the pope on stage, the right would have accused us of antisemitism and Hamas sympathies.”
It also comes at a time when the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague is coming under increasing pressure from the Trump administration. In July, Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowed to “dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, if necessary”, partly in response to the court’s investigation of Israeli officials.

articles.title_orig: Egypt train crash: At least seven killed and dozens injured
articles.title_zh: Egypt train crash: At least seven killed and dozens injured
articles.content_orig:
This live page has now closed - read more in our news story
At least seven people have died and dozens are injured after a train collision in al-Ayyat in Egypt's Giza governorate, the local health ministry says
A train driver is among those killed , the ministry adds - it's not yet clear what caused the collision
More than 70 ambulances have been deployed to the scene, officials say, with at least 112 people thought to have sustained injuries
Three hospitals are being used to treat the wounded, the health ministry says in its statement
Images show derailed train carriages with large crowds of people nearby, and Egyptian Red Crescent workers at the scene
This crash site has a long history of rail disasters, writes our reporter , including the country's deadliest when hundreds of people died in 2002 after a passenger train was engulfed in flames
At least seven people - including a driver - have been killed in a train collision in Egypt.
The country's health ministry says that 112 others have been injured and are being treated at three different hospitals near the crash site in al-Ayyat, south of Giza.
More than 70 ambulances were scrambled to the scene - authorities say the final number of fatalities is still being counted.
A train heading from Giza to Fayoum - south of Cairo - collided into the back of a service heading from Cairo to Aswan in the south, which is believed to have been stationary, according to Egypt's Public Prosecution Office.
The cause of the crash is yet to be officially determined and prosecutors have launched an investigation. Our reporter writes the site of the collision has a long history of rail disasters.
Images and footage from the scene show several derailed passenger carriages overturned along the tracks - you can watch that below.
We're now ending our live coverage, you can keep up to date in our news story.
Samantha Granville Middle East reporter
As well as this latest train collision, deadly rail disasters have also struck elsewhere in the country.
In August 2017, two passenger trains collided near the Mediterranean city of Alexandria, killing more than 40 people and injuring dozens.
Egypt was the first country in Africa and the Middle East to introduce railways. Today, around 110 million people rely on the network.
But while billions have been invested in roads and high-speed rail projects, much of the country's ageing railway infrastructure is still in need of modernisation.
Foreign leaders are expressing condolences and support for the victims of today's train collision in al-Ayyat, 73km (45 miles) south of Giza.
Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery.
The Turkish ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people.
Yemen's foreign ministry extends its condolences to those affected by the deadly train crash and Jordan's foreign ministry echoes the sentiment sharing its condolences.
Wael Hussein BBC News, reporting from Cairo
The two trains involved in Sunday's collision serve very different journeys â but both are important transport links for ordinary Egyptians.
The first was travelling to Fayoum, around 100km (62 miles) from Cairo, while the second was heading south to Aswan, nearly 900km (559 miles) away.
Both services are used largely by lower-income passengers, for whom train travel is one of the most affordable ways to get around the country. Tickets for the shorter journey cost less than $1, while the longer trip to Aswan costs less than $10.
Getting eyewitness accounts and personal testimonies can take time.
Many passengers on these services come from poorer communities and may not own smartphones, meaning photographs, videos and first-hand accounts of what happened can take longer to emerge.
More now from the Public Prosecution Office statement.
The office says that after an inspection of the scene, and speaking to eyewitnesses, they have determined that the front of the train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the back of the Cairo-Aswan rail service.
It adds that the train in front (Cairo-Aswan service) had stopped on the tracks. Both trains were heading in the same direction, the statement says.
On the number of deaths, the office says the final number of fatalities and injuries is still being counted but initial estimates say seven people, including the driver of the Giza to Fayoum train, died and 114 have been injured.
This figure differs slightly from the latest update from the country's health ministry, who say 112 people have been injured.
Egypt's public prosecutors have launched a formal investigation into the train collision that has killed at least seven people.
In a statement on Facebook, the Public Prosecution Office says it will work to determine the circumstances that caused the crash.
Investigators will examine the damaged carriages, tracks, surrounding area and work to identify any "shortcomings" in operational procedures and safety measures, the statement adds.
Youssef Taha BBC World Service News
Heavy machinery has been dispatched to the crash site to remove the overturned carriages
It's still unclear what caused the accident.
Heavy lifting equipment is at the scene and Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir is visiting the site.
There have been calls for him to resign such is the frequency of fatal train crashes in Egypt.
President Abdel-Fattah al-Sisi has ordered an urgent investigation saying that those responsible will be held accountable.
Samantha Granville Middle East reporter
More than 300 people were killed in a fire on a train travelling through the Giza governorate in 2002
The site of Sunday's accident in al-Ayyat, in Egypt's Giza governorate, has a long history of rail disasters.
It was the location of Egypt's deadliest train tragedy.
In February 2002, a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.
The train continued for around nine kilometres before coming to a halt. More than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.
Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.
More now from the health ministry's latest statement.
Egypt's Health Minister Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar continues to monitor the consequences of the train derailment, the statement says.
It adds that he has ordered all health facilities in the Giza and Beni Suef governorates to raise their level of preparedness and provide all necessary medical and emergency support to the injured.
Injuries sustained in the crash include bruising, fractured limbs, pelvis, and vertebrae and cuts to the head and face, the statement says.
"The remaining injured are continuing treatment under medical observation."
The number of people who have died following the train collision has risen to seven, with 112 others injured, according to the Egyptian health ministry.
It adds that 45 people who had been sent to hospital have now been discharged.
Earlier, the ministry reported four people - including a train driver - had been killed and 88 injured.
The Egyptian Red Crescent is at the scene of the crash, helping victims and their families.
The organisation says on its Facebook page that it dispatched teams from its headquarters, and branches in Giza, Fayoum and Beni Suef, to provide assistance and psychological support.
"The Egyptian Red Crescent, along with all its staff and volunteers, extends its deepest condolences and sympathy to the families of the victims," the post adds.
At least four people have been killed and dozens injured in a passenger train collision in Egypt, the country's health ministry says.
We don't know: what caused the crash, the identities of the other fatalities, the conditions of those in hospital or if there are still people in the carriages.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Some are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about the matter.
"The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers."
Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.
Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday requesting that he sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang .
The reports refer to Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.
Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, The New York Times first reported on Friday.
When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.
Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO's interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers, the Times reported .
Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump's Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.
Cornyn called the report "outrageous" in his post on X .
Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.
Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC's request for comment.

articles.title_orig: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.title_zh: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.content_orig:
South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic".
While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 30.76% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 64.82% 20 years ago.
The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections.
The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 24.64%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town. Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third overall with 9.76%, unseating the ANC as winner in the city of Durban, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), led by Julius Malema, once seen as a serious challenge to the ANC, came fourth with 6.22%.
"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC," said secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on Saturday. "We knew this disaster is coming, we're staring at it. As we got into elections, the cost of living of our people was too high. The middle class have turned on the ANC in big numbers."
Entering the count centre tonight, South Africa's president and leader of the ANC Cyril Ramaphosa said: "We accept the will of the people however concerning it might be, we accept that this is how the people of South Africa in our towns, in our cities, in our metros have spoken - and this is their verdict, we accept it with humility. It is a decline that is concerning, that is how I characterise it."
It's a continuing decline for the ANC, which lost majority rule in the national elections in 2024 for the first time in its history. It then had to form a coalition government with a raft of other parties in what is now known as the GNU, or government of national unity.
While the Democratic Alliance made significant gains in the cities in these local elections, its overall vote share rose marginally from 21.83% in 2021, and was below the 26.9% it gained in 2016.
Voter turnout was 52.29%, an increase from 45.9% in 2021, when elections were held during the Covid pandemic.
"This election is delivering a devastating message to the ANC", said political analyst Susan Booysen. "It's an ANC in decline at local municipal level, at the metropolitan level, and when the results are reflected provincially and nationally, we see severe declines in ANC levels of support all around."
The reason for that decline in support is largely due to poor service delivery and infrastructure across the country, from water and power to sanitation. "These are huge problems," says Booysen, "and have really been affecting the lives of ordinary people, in the suburbs, in the townships, and in very dramatic ways."
The big picture looks even more bleak for the ANC. The party will elect a new leader next year as Cyril Ramaphosa comes to end of his term. He is due to stay on as president of the country until the next national elections in 2029, but there are few candidates lined up to succeed him in either role.
"It is sort of the end of the liberation movement era in South Africa," said political analyst William Gumede, "and the dominance of the liberation movement since the end of apartheid. So the ANC is going to be a party that by 2029 could be the second biggest rather than the biggest party. It may actually spiral into a long period of just total infighting. This is a new era for South Africa's politics and also the ANC."
The elections also saw a significant shift in voting patterns, with the DA, traditionally known as the "white party" for attracting a largely white vote, gaining more black votes. "We're moving towards a post-racial voting pattern in South Africa," added Gumede.
South Africa now faces days of local coalition building, with the three metropolitan municipalities in the province of Gauteng, the country's powerhouse, under particular scrutiny. The ANC may even find itself shut out in the cities of Johannesburg and Pretoria.
"We are now in a coalition country," said Gumede. "Essentially, what the voters are saying is, "Well, the ANC has dominated the last three decades, they didn't use their power to change the society for the good, so we don't want the dominant parties anymore, whether at national level, provincial level, or rather now at a local level. We actually want coalitions. We want people to work together."
Parties now have 14 days from the moment results were announced to negotiate coalitions.

articles.title_orig: Motorola is quietly building apps and features that make Pixel and Samsung phones feel behind the times
articles.title_zh: Motorola is quietly building apps and features that make Pixel and Samsung phones feel behind the times
articles.content_orig:
I haven't thought much about Motorola since I dropped my Razr V3 several years back. After Android took over, a Google Pixel or a Samsung was always the easy pick for me.
That changed when I went through the spec sheet for Motorola's Signature flagship . The Signature 27 is due in November 2026 with features I didn't know I wanted.
So I dug through Motorola's announcement to see what it's promising and where Google and Samsung have an answer.
Google built its Tensor chips around on-device AI features and accepted slower raw performance to get there. The Signature 27 doesn't make the same trade.
Motorola uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, one of two 2nm chips Qualcomm announced at Snapdragon Summit in September 2026. Its two fastest cores run at up to 5.01GHz, while the Tensor G6 in the Pixel 11 Pro tops out at 4.11GHz.
Qualcomm says the Extreme chip has 13% faster CPU performance and a 44% faster GPU than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. That's the chip in the Galaxy S26 Ultra, which means Samsung's best phone uses an older chip until the next Galaxy launches.
Motorola also fitted six antennas, which it says double download speeds and help with cloud AI features.
The chip also helps with privacy, since its security features are a big reason GrapheneOS picked the Signature 27 as its first non-Pixel phone . Until now, GrapheneOS only officially supported Pixels.
Seven years of OS upgrades only keep Motorola level with Google and Samsung, which promise the same. What makes the promise believable this time is how early Motorola moved on Android 17.
It opened an Android 17 beta in February 2026 and started the stable rollout in August with the original Signature.
More than 50 Motorola phones are on the list, which is a big change for a brand I remember as slow with updates. It's the first Motorola flagship I'd expect to last as long as my Pixel.
A fast chip only stays fast while it's cool, because phone chips throttle when heat builds up. Most mainstream flagships handle this with a vapor chamber and stop there.
Gaming phones go further, and the Infinix GT 50 Pro even runs a liquid-cooling loop . The Signature 27 takes a middle route between the two.
Motorola's ArcticMesh system stacks diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapor chamber. Motorola says that the vapor chamber is 40% larger than the one in the original Signature.
It aims to maintain steady performance during gaming, AI tasks, and long video recordings. I'm still cautious, though, because a phone this thin can only dissipate so much heat.
Samsung puts a 200MP sensor on the Galaxy S26 Ultra's main camera. Motorola puts its 200MP sensor on the periscope telephoto, next to a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera.
Vivo and Xiaomi have shipped 200MP periscopes since 2024, so this isn't new to Android. However, Google and Samsung don't offer it on their flagships right now.
Super Zoom Pro pushes the range to 100x with generative AI. The Pixel 11 Pro reaches 120x, but its telephoto is 48MP, so it has fewer pixels to crop before AI fills in detail.
Motorola's zoom history makes me skeptical, so I want to see 30x samples before I give the 200MP sensor credit.
I'm more interested in video, since that's where Pixel has built its reputation. Motorola's Video Enhancement Engine analyzes the scene before and during recording, then adjusts color tones in real time.
Motorola pairs it with 3.5-degree OIS hardware and Qualcomm's image stabilization to keep handheld footage steady.
Pixel's Video Boost does its processing after you stop recording. Google processes the clip after it backs up to Google Photos, so you need an internet connection, and boosted recordings stop at 10 minutes.
If Motorola's real-time processing gets close to Video Boost quality, I'd take it over waiting on an upload after every concert.
Qira is Lenovo and Motorola's personal AI. It replaces Moto AI on supported phones with Android 17.
With your permission, it connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, and Outlook, and it can complete supported tasks for you. Its Catch Me Up feature gathers missed emails, chat updates, and calendar changes into one summary.
Lenovo says Qira runs on the device where it can, and it encrypts the personal information it stores locally.
Qira isn't exclusive to the Signature 27. Motorola's Android 17 rollout brings it to select Edge, Signature, and Razr phones, plus Lenovo PCs with 16GB of memory and the Moto Watch Ultra.
Qira's limit is that the full experience depends on owning Motorola or Lenovo hardware. The Signature 27 also ships with Gemini, so Qira has to do something Google's assistant can't on the same phone.
Qira also works alongside Smart Connect, Motorola's app for linking your phone to a PC, tablet, TV, or monitor. It handles file sharing and screen mirroring, and it connects to Windows 10 and 11 through a PC app.
Samsung and Pixel do something similar with Link to Windows. But, between Qira and Smart Connect, Motorola is building its own ecosystem on top of Android instead of leaving it all to Google.
None of this makes a Pixel or Galaxy obsolete, and plenty of Pixel owners won't switch even for GrapheneOS .
Still, a 2nm Snapdragon, a 200MP periscope, and real-time video tuning put pressure on Google and Samsung in areas they usually win.
Qira piques my interest the most, because a cross-device assistant that works well could push both companies to improve their own.
Motorola hasn't shared a US price, so I'll wait for the November reviews before deciding whether my next phone has a Motorola logo.

articles.title_orig: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100 others, authorities said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. One of the trains derailed, it said, but did not specify which.
The Health Ministry said at least four people were killed and 88 others were wounded. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, it said.
A train driver was among those killed in the collision, the Health Ministry said.
President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post he is following the aftermath of the train collision "with great concern and extend my deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."
"I have directed state agencies to provide the necessary medical care, promptly investigate the circumstances of the accident and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent," he wrote.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian Railway Authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

Le Soleil newspaper said that most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.

articles.title_orig: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
articles.title_zh: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
articles.content_orig:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been given the opportunity to form a new government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections, raising the possibility of an end to his long tenure in power.
President Isaac Herzog selected the former military chief on Saturday, following consultations with political parties. Eisenkot has 28 days to cobble together a coalition to form a government. If he fails to form a new administration within that period, he can seek a 14-day extension.
“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, posted on X.
However, the 66-year-old faces a difficult challenge as many of the opposition parties hold sharply conflicting positions on national security, religion and the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has a 61-seat majority in Israel’s 120-member parliament, the Knesset.
As a result, Arab-led parties hold a potentially decisive role in determining who governs Israel, even as Eisenkot and his prospective partners refuse to rely on their support.
So what do we now know about Eisenkot’s possible paths to power, and can he succeed in unseating Netanyahu?
Eisenkot’s potential coalition spans his Yashar party, the centre-left Democrats led by Yair Golan, Naftali Bennett’s centre-right Together party and Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu (Israel Our Home).
Overall, they control 48 seats, well short of a majority.
Arab-led parties Ra’am (United List) and the Joint List (comprising three parties – Hadash, Ta’al and Balad) – jointly holding 19 seats – have endorsed Eisenkot’s attempt to form a government. Their backing would give the broader anti-Netanyahu camp a combined 67 seats.
Hadash is an Arab-Jewish party, Ta’al advocates for the rights of Palestinian citizens of Israel, and Balad demands equal rights for all its citizens.
However, Eisenkot has ruled out bringing Arab parties into his government, while Lieberman has repeatedly rejected forming a minority administration dependent on their support. Golan’s Democrats have been more willing to partner with Ra’am and the Joint List.
“We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” Golan said after the election.
Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition has fallen from the 64 seats it secured in 2022 to 53, eight seats short of a majority.
His Likud is the largest individual party with 27 seats, while Eisenkot’s Yashar won 21.
Netanyahu’s efforts to remain in power suffered a further setback when United Torah Judaism, a longtime ultra-Orthodox ally, declined to endorse him or any other candidate during consultations with Herzog.
While the decision hurts Netanyahu’s prospects of regaining power, it did not rule out the party supporting him in future coalition negotiations if their demands were met, particularly compulsory military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews, which they reject.
If Eisenkot is unable to put together a coalition, he could potentially lead a minority government backed by Arab parties from outside.
A minority government is formed when the parties holding cabinet positions do not collectively control a majority of seats in parliament. Instead, they depend on support from lawmakers outside the governing coalition to remain in power and pass legislation.
Eisenkot could establish such an administration with his four-party bloc relying on external parliamentary support from Ra’am and the Joint List .
Under this arrangement, the Arab-led parties would not necessarily receive cabinet positions or formally join the coalition.
They could instead negotiate policy concessions in exchange for their parliamentary support.
In 2021, Ra’am joined a government led by Bennett, becoming the first independent Arab party to participate in an Israeli governing coalition.
That administration collapsed after 18 months, mainly due to disagreements over the illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and Palestinian statehood. Most Israeli parties do not support the creation of a sovereign Palestinian state as part of the so-called two-state solution.
Netanyahu, who has been in power for most of the past 20 years, has openly rejected Palestinian statehood and has pushed settlement expansions that are the biggest hurdles in the realisation of Palestinian statehood. Settlements are considered illegal under international law.
Beyond a minority government, Eisenkot could attempt to secure a parliamentary majority by bringing Israel’s two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, into his coalition.
Together, they hold 13 seats, which would give Eisenkot’s bloc exactly the 61 seats required for a majority.
However, such an alliance would require compromises over military conscription exemptions for ultra-Orthodox religious students, an issue that has long divided Israeli politics.
Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have criticised the exemptions. But Lieberman has recently indicated that he is open to compromise.
While United Torah Judaism has refused to endorse Netanyahu, Shas backed the beleaguered prime minister.
Another option would be a unity government involving Eisenkot’s Yashar, Bennett’s Together party, Lieberman’s Israel Our Home and Netanyahu’s Likud.
Such an alliance would command 67 seats, but would require Eisenkot and his partners to abandon their central election pledge to remove Netanyahu from power.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the required time, Herzog could give Netanyahu an opportunity to form a governing coalition.
Should both leaders fail, parliament could nominate another candidate. If no government emerges after a process lasting 100 days, Israelis could be heading to the polls again.
The negotiations could determine not only who becomes Israel’s next prime minister, but also which political parties control key ministries and shape policies on the economy, military conscription and the occupied Palestinian territory.
Several members of Eisenkot’s opposition bloc have previously held senior government positions, including in the coalition that removed Netanyahu from power in 2021.
Bennett, who served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022, has long opposed the establishment of a Palestinian state and advocated annexing large parts of the occupied West Bank.
During Israel’s 11-day war on Gaza in May 2021, Bennett, then an opposition politician, backed Netanyahu’s military offensive in the Palestinian enclave. More than 250 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks.
Meanwhile, Lieberman served as finance minister in Bennett’s government and previously held the defence portfolio under Netanyahu.
He previously proposed swapping some Arab communities in Israel proper for Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank in the context of a final peace deal with the Palestinians.
Lieberman’s party backs illegal settlement expansion, including E1, and annexing all of Area C, 60 percent of the occupied West Bank already under full Israeli control. E1, which stands for East 1 settlement, is a 12sq km corridor with thousands of housing units. It will cut the West Bank into two parts.
Eisenkot himself served in Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet before leaving the government after disagreements over the conduct of the genocide in Gaza. He has not opposed the genocide but criticised Netanyahu for prioritising his political survival over security considerations.
He has called the idea of a Palestinian state “delusional”, and he supports “strengthening” illegal settlements.
Academic Neve Gordon says an Eisenkot government could bring notable changes to Israel’s domestic politics, particularly by reversing parts of Netanyahu’s judicial overhaul.

articles.title_orig: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
articles.title_zh: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
articles.content_orig:
South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments.
With all votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had just over 30 percent nationally against about 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA).
That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance.
Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties.
While still the largest party in South Africa, the ANC’s support has steadily eroded as voters grow increasingly frustrated with corruption and the party’s failure to tackle unemployment, which tops 34 percent more than three decades after the end of apartheid.
Failures in basic services, such as water and electricity, have also contributed to the ANC’s vote share falling in local elections over the past 15 years.
The party failed to win an outright majority in any of the eight major metro areas, including Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Since no party won more than 50 percent of the votes in many cities, including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up or hash it out with smaller parties to form municipal governments.
Parties will have 14 days to negotiate before city councils are formed.
ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the result “catastrophic” for the ANC but said the party would not go begging for positions when coalition talks begin soon.
“When the people tell us we have fallen short, … the honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order,” Mbalula said on Saturday.
In Johannesburg, the DA led the count with about 35 percent of the votes, compared with 20 percent for the ANC.
That could give DA veteran Helen Zille, who campaigned on fixing potholes and leaking water pipes, a good chance of becoming mayor, depending on the coalition agreements reached.
The DA said in a statement that it would initiate coalition discussions with “political parties that share a commitment to clean and accountable government, rooting out corruption, service delivery for all, the rule of law, and non-racialism”.
